topic_ko: 위협받는 석유 — 혁신이 에너지 지형을 재편하다
_note: 원문 유형은 장문 제목+어휘. title 과 vocab 유형을 가장 강하게 출제. 유형마다 passage 를 다르게 paraphrase.

passage: Transport is the single largest consumer of oil.
Because oil is costly, today's car engines burn fuel far more efficiently than those of decades ago.
If oil prices climb still higher, fuel cell technology will gain fresh momentum.
The big car multinationals have already built prototype motors and are racing to cut costs.
Their future profits depend on getting there first.
Now imagine a true breakthrough in fuel cell technology.
Oil prices would fall sharply, and oil companies and OPEC would lose much income.
Because this threat is real, producers are diversifying into other industries to survive.
choices: why electric cars will never replace gasoline vehicles
how OPEC sets the global price of crude oil each year
how high oil prices drive innovation that reshapes the energy landscape
why transport uses less oil than heavy manufacturing
how fuel cells were first invented in the laboratory
theme.explanation_ko: 비싼 유가가 효율적 엔진과 연료전지 기술 혁신을 촉진하고, 그 결과 석유 기업·OPEC이 다른 산업으로 다각화한다는 내용. ③이 주제.
theme.distractor_ko: ①전기차, ②OPEC 가격 결정, ④운송의 석유 소비량 비교, ⑤연료전지 발명사는 초점이 아니다.

passage: We should see high oil prices not as a curse but as a spur to innovation.
Costly oil has already made car engines far more efficient and far less polluting.
Should prices rise further, fuel cell technology will surge ahead.
Carmakers are racing to perfect prototype motors because their futures depend on it.
If a breakthrough comes, oil prices will collapse and oil revenue will shrink.
Producers know this, so they are seeking alternative sources of income.
We must recognize that innovation, not price control, will decide the energy future.
The wise oil majors are already becoming energy companies rather than oil companies.
choices: 정부는 유가를 인위적으로 낮게 유지해야 한다.
석유 기업은 다른 산업으로의 진출을 피해야 한다.
연료전지 기술은 결코 상용화되지 못할 것이다.
운송 부문의 석유 소비는 줄일 수 없다.
혁신이 에너지의 미래를 결정하므로 높은 유가는 변화의 자극제로 보아야 한다.
claim.explanation_ko: 높은 유가가 효율·연료전지 혁신을 자극하고 혁신이 에너지 미래를 결정하므로, 유가 상승을 자극제로 보아야 한다는 주장. ⑤.
claim.distractor_ko: ①유가 통제, ②진출 회피, ③연료전지 불가능, ④소비 불가축소는 본문 주장과 다르다.

passage: The biggest user of oil is the transport sector.
High oil prices have already pushed car engines toward far greater fuel efficiency.
If prices rise further, fuel cell technology, which makes energy from water, will accelerate.
Carmakers have built prototypes and are competing to lower costs and raise performance.
Imagine a real fuel cell breakthrough.
Oil prices would fall dramatically, cutting the income of oil firms and OPEC.
Facing this threat, producers are hunting for alternative sources of income.
The oil majors are diversifying, becoming energy companies more than oil companies.
choices: 전기차의 보급이 유가 하락의 유일한 원인이다.
높은 유가가 혁신을 촉진하고, 그 혁신이 석유 산업의 다각화를 부른다.
운송 부문은 석유를 거의 사용하지 않는다.
연료전지는 물 대신 석유로 에너지를 만든다.
OPEC은 다른 산업 진출을 거부하고 있다.
gist.explanation_ko: 비싼 유가 → 효율·연료전지 혁신 → 유가 하락 위협 → 석유 기업의 다각화로 이어지는 흐름이 요지. ②.
gist.distractor_ko: ①전기차 단일 원인, ③운송 무사용, ④연료전지 원료 오류, ⑤진출 거부는 요지가 아니다.

passage: Oil's largest customer has always been transport.
But costly oil has quietly transformed the internal combustion engine.
Cars today sip fuel far more efficiently than those of 1972.
Push prices higher and fuel cell technology, drawing energy from water, gathers momentum.
Carmakers are already racing to bring prototype motors to market.
Picture a genuine breakthrough: oil prices would tumble.
Oil firms and OPEC would lose vast income.
So they are moving into new industries, reshaping the whole energy landscape.
choices: Why Transport Will Always Depend on Crude Oil
OPEC's Tight Grip on the World's Fuel Prices
The History of the Internal Combustion Engine
When Costly Oil Sparks Innovation That Redraws the Energy Map
Why Fuel Cells Are Too Expensive to Matter
title.explanation_ko: 비싼 유가가 혁신(효율 엔진·연료전지)을 촉발하고 그것이 에너지 지형을 재편한다는 흐름을 압축한 ④가 제목.
title.distractor_ko: ①운송의 영구 석유 의존, ②OPEC의 가격 장악, ③엔진의 역사, ⑤연료전지 무용론은 글의 핵심과 어긋난다.

passage: Because oil is expensive, engineers have made car engines steadily more efficient.
If oil climbs higher still, fuel cell technology will gain yet more momentum.
Carmakers have built prototype motors and race to cut their costs.
Their future profits depend upon it.
Now imagine a breakthrough: oil prices would fall dramatically.
Oil companies and OPEC would stand to lose much income.
The fact that this threat is real is driving producers to look elsewhere.
The 'oil majors' are now more energy companies than oil companies.
implication.underlined: more energy companies than oil companies
choices: they have broadened beyond oil into the wider energy business
they have stopped producing oil altogether
they now sell electricity directly to households
they have merged with national governments
they refuse to invest in any new technology
implication.explanation_ko: '석유 회사라기보다 에너지 회사'라는 표현은 석유에 머무르지 않고 더 넓은 에너지 사업으로 사업 영역을 넓혔음을 뜻한다. ①.
implication.distractor_ko: ②석유 생산 완전 중단, ③가정용 전기 직판, ④정부와 합병, ⑤기술 투자 거부는 모두 본문과 다르다.

passage: The major consumer of oil is transport.
Because oil is expensive, car engines today are far more efficient than they were in 1972.
In fact, if the price of oil does rise much further, fuel cell technology will receive yet another momentum.
The big car multinationals have already produce the prototype motors.
They are currently racing to try and get prices down and engine performances up.
Imagine now if there is a breakthrough in fuel cell technology.
Oil prices would fall dramatically, signalling much less demand than supply.
The fact that this threat is real is driving the producers to look for alternative sources of income.
grammar._grammar_note: ③ 'have already produce' 가 비문법. 현재완료는 'have + 과거분사' 이므로 'have already produced' 가 옳다.
grammar.explanation_ko: 현재완료는 'have + 과거분사' 구조이므로 ③은 'have already produced' 가 되어야 한다. 원형 'produce' 는 비문법. ③이 정답.
grammar.distractor_ko: ① 비교급 강조 more efficient, ② 강조 조동사 does rise, ④ 분사구문 signalling, ⑤ drive + 목적어 + to부정사 to look 은 모두 옳다.

passage: The major consumer of oil is transport.
Because oil is expensive, car engines today are far more efficient in their consumption of fuel than they were in 1972.
If the price of oil rises much further, fuel cell technology will receive yet another setback.
The big car multinationals have already produced prototype motors, racing to get prices down and performance up.
Now imagine a breakthrough in fuel cell technology.
Oil prices would fall dramatically, signalling much less demand than supply.
Oil companies and OPEC producers would stand to lose much income.
Driven by this real threat, the OPEC countries are urgently attempting to embrace other industries.
vocab._vocab_note: ② 'setback' 가 의도적 오답. 유가가 더 오르면 연료전지 기술은 '추진력(momentum)'을 얻게 되므로 '차질(setback)'은 정반대이다.
vocab.explanation_ko: 유가가 더 오르면 연료전지 기술은 또 다른 '추진력(momentum)'을 받는다는 맥락이므로 ② 'setback(차질)'은 정반대의 낱말이다. ②가 정답.
vocab.distractor_ko: ①효율적인 ③극적으로 ④잃다 ⑤진출/포용(embrace)은 문맥상 모두 적절하다.

passage: Because oil is expensive, today's car engines are far more efficient than those of 1972.
If oil prices rise much further, fuel cell technology will gain yet more momentum.
Carmakers have built prototype motors and race to cut costs because their profits depend on it.
Now imagine a breakthrough in fuel cell technology, and ask what would happen to oil prices.
They would fall dramatically, signalling much less demand than supply.
Oil companies and OPEC producers would stand to lose much income.
Because this threat is real, producers are seeking alternative sources of income.
The oil majors have diversified, becoming energy companies more than oil companies.
blank.explanation_ko: 연료전지 혁신으로 석유 수요가 공급보다 훨씬 줄어들면 가격은 '극적으로 하락(fall dramatically)'하며, 뒤이어 기업·OPEC이 수입을 잃는다고 했다. ⑤.
blank.distractor_ko: ①꾸준히 상승 ②변동 없음 ③하룻밤에 두 배 ④천천히 회복은 'much less demand than supply' 와 '수입 손실' 단서에 맞지 않는다.

irrelevant.intro: Because oil is expensive, car engines today are far more efficient in their consumption of fuel than they were in 1972.
sentences: Many drivers enjoy listening to music or podcasts during their daily commute to work.
If the price of oil rises much further, fuel cell technology, which produces energy from water, will receive yet another momentum.
The big car multinationals have already produced prototype motors and are racing to get prices down and performance up.
If there were a breakthrough in fuel cell technology, oil prices would fall dramatically, and oil companies and OPEC would lose much income.
Because this threat is real, the oil majors have diversified and are now more energy companies than oil companies.
irrelevant.explanation_ko: 글은 '유가·연료전지 혁신 → 유가 하락 위협 → 석유 기업 다각화'의 흐름인데 ① '운전자들이 통근 중 음악·팟캐스트를 즐긴다'는 무관하다.
irrelevant.distractor_ko: ②③④⑤는 모두 유가·혁신·석유 산업 다각화라는 주제로 연결된다.

order.given: The major consumer of oil is transport. Because oil is expensive, car engines today are far more efficient in their consumption of fuel than they were in 1972.

blocks.A: Imagine now if there is a breakthrough in fuel cell technology. Oil prices would fall dramatically, and oil companies and OPEC producers would stand to lose much income.
blocks.B: In fact, if the price of oil rises much further, fuel cell technology will receive yet another momentum. The big car multinationals have already produced prototype motors, since their future profits depend upon it.
blocks.C: The fact that this threat is real is driving the producers to look for alternative sources of income. The 'oil majors' are now more energy companies than oil companies these days.

order.explanation_ko: 주어진 글의 '효율적 엔진'을 (B)가 'In fact ... 연료전지 추진력'으로 잇고, (A)가 'Imagine ... 혁신 시 유가 폭락'으로 발전시키며, (C)가 'this threat(그 위협)'을 받아 다각화로 결론짓는다. (B)-(A)-(C).
order.distractor_ko: (C)의 'this threat'은 (A)의 유가 폭락 위협을 가리키므로 그 뒤라야 하고, (A)의 'Imagine' 가정은 (B)의 연료전지 추진력 언급 뒤에 자연스럽다.

insert.insert_sentence: Imagine now if there is a breakthrough in fuel cell technology.

passage_marked.text: Because oil is expensive, car engines today are far more efficient than they were in 1972.
If the price of oil rises much further, fuel cell technology will receive yet another momentum.
The big car multinationals have already produced prototype motors, racing to get prices down.
Oil prices would fall dramatically, and oil companies and OPEC producers would stand to lose much income.
Because this threat is real, the oil majors have diversified into other industries.

insert.explanation_ko: 주어진 문장은 '연료전지 기술의 돌파구를 상상해 보라'는 가정 도입이고, 그 가정의 결과인 ④ '유가가 극적으로 하락한다'가 바로 뒤따라야 자연스럽다. ④가 정답.
insert.distractor_ko: ④에 넣지 않으면 'Oil prices would fall dramatically' 의 가정법 귀결이 가리킬 전제(돌파구 상상)가 앞에 오지 않는다.

passage: Transport is the largest consumer of oil.
Because oil is expensive, car engines have grown far more fuel-efficient.
Higher prices would give fuel cell technology fresh momentum.
Carmakers race to perfect prototype motors.
A real breakthrough would send oil prices tumbling.
Oil companies and OPEC would lose much income.
Facing this threat, producers seek new sources of income.
The oil majors are becoming energy companies rather than oil companies.
summary.summary_template: High oil prices push __(A)__ in engines and fuel cells, and the resulting threat drives oil producers to __(B)__ into other industries.
summary.explanation_ko: 높은 유가는 엔진·연료전지의 (A)혁신(innovation)을 촉진하고, 그 위협은 석유 생산자를 다른 산업으로 (B)다각화하게(diversify) 만든다. ④.
summary.distractor_ko: (A)는 stagnation/decline 이 아니라 innovation, (B)는 retreat/withdraw 가 아니라 diversify 여야 한다.

writing.question: 다음 우리말과 같은 뜻이 되도록 <보기>의 단어를 모두 배열하여 영작하시오.
writing.answer: The major consumer of oil is transport.
writing.explanation_ko: 주어 The major consumer of oil + 동사 is + 보어 transport.

writing.question: 다음 우리말과 같은 뜻이 되도록 <보기>의 단어를 모두 배열하여 영작하시오.
writing.ko_prompt: 석유가 비싸기 때문에, 오늘날의 자동차 엔진은 훨씬 더 효율적이다.
writing.answer: Because oil is expensive, car engines today are far more efficient.
writing.explanation_ko: 이유 부사절 Because oil is expensive + 주절, 비교급 강조 far more efficient.

writing.question: 다음 우리말을 <조건>에 맞게 영작하시오.
writing.ko_prompt: 만약 연료전지 기술에 돌파구가 생긴다면, 석유 가격은 극적으로 하락할 것이다.
conditions: 가정을 나타내는 if 절을 사용할 것
writing.answer: If there is a breakthrough in fuel cell technology, oil prices would fall dramatically.
writing.explanation_ko: if 조건절 + 주절 would + fall dramatically(극적으로 하락하다).

writing.question: 다음 글을 읽고, 흐름상 빈칸에 들어갈 한 단어를 본문에서 찾아 쓰시오.
writing.context: Facing the real threat of falling oil prices, the oil majors have ___________ and are now more energy companies than oil companies.
writing.explanation_ko: 본문에서 석유 대기업들은 사업을 '다각화하여(diversified)' 에너지 회사가 되었다.

writing.question: 다음 밑줄 친 문장을 우리말로 해석하시오.
writing.en_prompt: The fact that this threat is real is driving the producers to look for alternative sources of income.
writing.answer: 이 위협이 실재한다는 사실이 생산자들로 하여금 대체 수입원을 찾도록 몰아가고 있다.
writing.explanation_ko: The fact that ...(~라는 사실), drive + 목적어 + to부정사(~가 …하도록 몰아가다), alternative sources of income(대체 수입원).

writing.question: 다음 글을 읽고, 요약문의 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 단어를 본문에 근거하여 쓰시오.
writing.summary: Expensive oil drives (A)___________ in engine and fuel cell technology, and the threat of falling prices pushes oil producers to (B)___________ into other industries.
writing.explanation_ko: (A) 비싼 유가는 기술 '혁신(innovation)'을 촉진한다. (B) 유가 하락 위협은 생산자를 '다각화하게(diversify)' 만든다.
